title: Cross-domain anchor sampling with recency bias for calibration pack generation (INT8/FP8)
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Goal: produce per-domain calibration packs that maximize representativeness for production traffic while preserving headroom for low-volume domains and temporal generalization. We will build a sampling pipeline that combines cross-domain anchor examples, recency-weighted reservoir sampling, and deterministic temporal holdouts for validation. Packs should be consumable by the quant calibration toolchain for both INT8 and FP8 profile generation, and by the accuracy validation harness used by Evals.

Motivation: existing pack strategies overfit on long-tail static exemplars or on coarse stratification; this causes calibration drift when traffic patterns change or when small domains have rare but important prompt shapes. We need a reproducible, explainable sampling policy that balances (1) recent traffic signal, (2) stable anchor exemplars per domain, and (3) synthetic augmentation for underrepresented token shapes.

Non-goals: this ticket does not change model-level quant rules or runtime kernel selection; it focuses on dataset curation and sampling strategy only.
proposed_solution:
1) Domain grouping: map production prompts to domain tags via existing fingerprinting service. Use a two-tier grouping: primary domain (business vertical) + sub-cohort (API surface or intent bucket).
2) Anchor selection: for each primary domain, select a set of deterministic anchors (N_anchor=25 by default) using embedding k-centers on the last 90 days of traffic; anchors are persisted and versioned.
3) Recency-weighted reservoir: stream recent traffic (30d window) and perform reservoir sampling per-domain with a time-decay weight (half-life = 7 days) so recent examples are more likely to be selected; cap per-domain contribution proportional to 1 + log(traffic_volume) to avoid dominating packs.
4) Low-volume handling: if domain volume < threshold (T=500 requests/month), supplement with synthetic paraphrases of anchors (using small prompt templates) and include cross-domain similar anchors identified via embedding nearest-neighbors.
5) Deterministic temporal holdouts: reserve the last 7 days as a validation holdout for accuracy regression testing; ensure no leakage by hashing request ids with seed tied to pack version.
6) Pack construction: combine anchors + reservoir sample + synthetic augmentations into a per-domain pack and produce metadata file with provenance, sampling parameters, and token distribution histograms.
7) Output: JSONL packs with fields (request_id, prompt, response_stub, domain, cohort, sampling_tag, embedding_id, pack_version). Provide helper tooling to convert into calibration tool input format and Evals harness format.
acceptance_criteria: Automated pipeline produces per-domain packs for top 200 domains (by 30d volume) within the release cycle
Each pack includes: persisted anchors, recency-weighted reservoir examples, synthetic augmentation for low-volume domains, and a validation holdout slice
Calibration runs (INT8 and FP8) using these packs must have reproducible profiles (seeded) and produce a delta report compared to baseline within expected ranges
Evals accuracy runs on holdout show no >2% drop in top-line metric for priority domains post-quantization (or documented mitigation plan)
Metadata files and sampling parameters are stored in the artifact registry and referenced by PRs/rollouts
test_plan:
1) Unit tests for anchor selection and recency-weighted reservoir logic (edge cases: domain volume=0, steady traffic bursts).
2) Smoke run: generate packs for 10 high-volume and 10 low-volume domains; run internal quant calibration and Evals on holdouts.
3) Simulation: synthetic traffic replay to validate sampling distribution over 90d windows and verify recency bias behaves as expected (plots).
4) Canary: deploy to staging calibration jobs; compare INT8/FP8 profiles against current baseline and check for regressions.
5) Rollout: gated by automated metric checks and manual sign-off from Applied ML and Runtime teams.

2026-02-28 Naomi Ruiz (Applied ML): Reviewed prototype; requested stronger encryption of persisted anchors when stored for Private deployments and an access control note in metadata. Added to dependencies.

2026-03-01 Design review (Sofia Martinez): Provided feedback on pack metadata UI to show sampling rationale in Console; suggested adding a human-readable 'why-this-example' blurb generated from prompt analysis.
